J1_line_asserts_challenged_proposition.justification: The response challenges 'If hgP = gP then P = ghg^{-1}P (i.e., ghg^{-1} in P).' First-choice line 27 asserts exactly that chain: 'Then for every h in H, we have hgP = gP, which is equivalent to P = ghg^(-1)P, which is equivalent to ghg^(-1) being an element of P.' Under the source's active assumptions (line 13: |G| = p^r m, p not dividing m, P a Sylow p-subgroup; line 15: H a p-subgroup; line 23: H acts on G/P by left multiplication; line 25: gP is a fixed point of that action) line 27 is the step that converts the fixed-point property into membership in P, and the direction of conjugation is precisely what the response disputes.

J2_evidence_specified.justification: A concrete finite instance with every object named: 'In G = S3, let P = <(12)>, H = <(13)>, g = (123) and h = (23); we have hgP = gP but ghg^{-1} = (13) not in P.' The group, the subgroup, and the two elements entering the disputed equivalence are all explicit; one defect of specification is recorded under J3 (the named H does not contain the h that is used).

J3_evidence_check.justification: Exact enumeration of S_3 in scripts/P31_check.py confirms the supplied data: with P = {e,(12)}, g = (123), h = (23), the coset hgP = {(13),(123)} equals gP = {(123),(13)}, so line 27's antecedent holds, while ghg^{-1} = (13) is not in P, so line 27's asserted equivalent 'P = ghg^{-1}P, i.e. ghg^{-1} in P' fails; the script also shows the correct consequent g^{-1}hg = (12) does lie in P, which is the conjugation direction line 27 reverses. Defect in the witness, stated and not repaired: the response names H = <(13)> but uses h = (23), which is not in that H, and the script confirms that for H = <(13)> the coset gP is not fixed; so as literally written the triple is not an instance of the source's 'for every h in H' scope. The refutation nevertheless stands on the supplied elements, because what line 27 asserts and the response's claim quantifies over is the equivalence hgP = gP <-> ghg^{-1} in P for group elements, and the supplied P, g, h falsify it; the script records (as information, not as a substituted witness) that the very same P, g, h also form a full instance of the source's configuration when the p-subgroup is the one generated by the h actually used.

J4_consequence_overreach.justification: The emitted JSON contains only the candidate label 0027, the claim and the counterexample; no consequence is drawn. The visible scratch reasoning adds only that line 29 ('This proves that gHg^(-1) is a subset of P') inherits the error and that 0027 is the root, which is a localization remark rather than a consequence; at no point does the response assert that the second Sylow theorem itself is false.

notes: Arithmetic in S_3 is fully verified; the one point for a second reader or adjudicator is the witness's internal mismatch (H named as <(13)> while h = (23) is used). A reader who insists on the source's 'for every h in H' scope may prefer to treat that as a failed assumption; a reader who reads the disputed object as the equivalence itself will see an exact refutation. Note also the conjugation convention: the check uses (p*q)(i) = p(q(i)), the standard convention under which the response's computations are the ones reproduced.
